operators.caption: sum and difference, read left to right: a - b - c is (a - b) - c
product and quotient, tighter than a sum, read left to right
a product may leave out its * after a number or a closing parenthesis, not after a name
minus, tighter than a product and looser than a power: -x^2 is -(x^2)
a power: a whole n from 1 to 64 is a product of n factors; any other b, a^b for a > 0 (a^0 is 1)
an equation in one unknown, solved for it

constants.name: nan
constants.caption: not a number: what a function gives outside its domain

questions.caption: an expression, evaluated, its digits proved
an equation in one unknown: in closed form with its steps where it is a quadratic, and every real root proved
every root on the interval, each proved alone in its own
a parameter: a row below that reads it is answered as a function of p, synthesised and certified
an integral; a limit may be a parameter above
questions.example:
x in [0.5, 6]
Si = integral sin(t)/t dt on [0, x]

routes.name: evaluate
routes.caption: Evaluated as written, with nothing rewritten: in fractions where every operation is one on fractions, else in intervals, each number held as it was typed and every operation rounding outward, so the true value lies between the ends; the digits both ends share are proved.

routes.name: expression
routes.caption: The expression as written, a function of the parameter it reads.

routes.name: closed form
routes.caption: Solved in closed form. The coefficients are read from the equation's own values and the degree is checked at more points; the roots come from the quadratic formula in the form that keeps the small root, and Vieta's formulas check them by a second route.

routes.name: linear system
routes.caption: Solved by elimination. Each equation's coefficients are read from its own values and that it is linear is checked at more points; in fractions where every coefficient is one, so the solution is exact, else in doubles.

routes.name: interval method
routes.caption: The interval method. The axis is cut where the inequality is undecided on a piece, computed in intervals, until every piece is proved to hold it or not; between a piece where it holds and one where it does not is a root of its left side less its right, proved alone there by Newton's interval step and an end of the set, or a break where it has no value.

routes.name: every root, proved
routes.caption: Every root on the box, each proved. The box is cut in two where it is undecided; a piece is excluded where the equation's interval leaves out zero, and holds exactly one root where Newton's step in intervals, with the derivative enclosed by a dual number, lands inside it. Where the derivative may vanish, at a double root, nothing is proved. With no bracket the box is every double.

routes.name: root on a bracket
routes.caption: A root where the equation changes sign on its bracket, by bisection to the last bit.

routes.name: integral
routes.caption: The integral by the library's quadrature, its error estimated, not proved.

routes.name: synthesis
routes.caption: Synthesised. The library computes the question's value at each parameter by its own solvers; the answer is the shortest expression in the parameter that matches it, searched bottom up, or a Chebyshev polynomial where none of a few terms does, checked against those values on a dense grid.
